edges.rationale: Understanding the two-component structure of RAG is necessary to compare it against finetuning and determine when each approach is appropriate.
Knowledge of how retrievers fetch context and generators produce responses is required to evaluate factual consistency between generated responses and retrieved context.
Understanding the retriever-generator structure is a prerequisite for making practical implementation decisions such as starting with BM25 or using vector databases.
Guidance on choosing between RAG and finetuning informs practical recommendations for beginning RAG implementations and when full context inclusion may eliminate the need for RAG.
